newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU backs Italy's EMU plan, urges further action.
newsitem.headline: EU backs Italy's EMU plan, urges further action.

text.p: The European Union on Monday welcomed Italy's efforts to join its single currency but urged Rome to adopt further measures to reform its welfare state.

EU finance ministers said that the economic assumptions underlying Italy's convergence plan were "reasonable" but also dependent on low inflation and the "successful implementation of...structural budgetary adjustment."

The plan unveiled at a meeting of the bloc's 15 finance ministers foresees the Italian government bringing its 1997 public deficit down to three percent of Gross Domestic Product, the Maastricht Treaty's target.
While the group said Rome had reaffirmed its commitment to monetary union in presenting the plan, it was most important that the government take further action.
"Of crucial importance is the reform of the welfare state," the ministers concluded.

Within this area, Italy should strive to keep expenditure on pensions constant relative to GDP growth and reform the current tax system. Special attention should also be paid to "the avoidance of revenue shortfalls."
